name: Antonyuk v. James
summary: The Second Circuit evaluated New York's Concealed Carry Improvement Act passed after Bruen, upholding some provisions and striking others, demonstrating the contested scope of permissible firearm regulations under the historical tradition framework.
significance: This Second Circuit decision addressed New York's post-Bruen carry law and illustrates how the lower courts have been grappling with the application of Bruen to permitting and carry restrictions, providing relevant circuit-level analysis.
